To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DAE δ A LUS project can be realized by using a high intensity H 2 + injector cyclotron and a space charge dominated ring cyclotron.

1. the injector cyclotron can accelerate and extract a 5 ma beam with a low beam loss on the septum and 2. the ring cyclotron can accelerate a 5 MA beam to 800 MeV with a low beam emittance and no space charge induced losses.
the space charge effects are negligible in the ring cyclotron, but the space charge effects in the injector cyclotron can be mitigated by a careful optimization of the magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and the simulation of the beam dynamics for the DAE δALUS project.
the development of a new type of high intensity cyclotron, the DAE δALUS cyclotron, which will accelerate protons from 2 MeV to 800 MeVs with an average power of the order of MWs.
the design and optimization of the high intensity cyclotrons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DAE δ A LUS project is technically feasible.
the DAE δ Alus ring cyclotron is space charge dominated, but that it is well designed to cope with space charge induced beam losses.
the DAE δALUS project is feasible from a beam dynamics point of view, but that the space charge effects in the injector cyclotron should be taken into account for the final beam dynamics design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the beam dynamics simulations for the injector cyclotron show that the beam is space charge dominated and a beam current of 5 mA is possible, while the simulations for the ring cyclotron show that no beam loss occurs during acceleration and extraction and that the space charge is not a dominant issue.
the DAEδAL US ring cyclotron can be operated at 10 mA without space charge induced beam losses.
space charge does not limit the beam current of the ring cyclotron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
space charge effects are negligible for the beam dynamics in the ring cyclotron.
the space charge effects can be mitigated by the choice of an adequate beam optics.
the ring cyclotron can efficiently accelerate a 5 MA beam with a low emittance.
